text:
alex: Quick followup from the RFC — we proposed a 'translation shim' between Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Need to decide whether it stays thin (routing + auth mapping) or becomes a full agent that handles KMS, local metrics, and rollout logic. Opinions?

maria: My 2c: keep it thin where possible. Simpler to maintain and less attack surface for Hosted. Private customers can opt-in to a local agent with extra connectors.

sanjay: Thin is nice but remember air-gapped/private means control plane can't reach into customer network. If translation requires external keys or callbacks, thin won't work there.

kevin: Agreed with both. We should formalize a capability matrix and an automated translator that emits a deployment manifest per mode. Example mapping sketch:
```json
{
  "auth": { "hosted": "token", "private": "mTLS" },
  "kms": { "hosted": "redwood-managed", "private": "customer-endpoint" }
}
```
This keeps the runtime stable and makes conversions auditable.

alex: Two immediate tradeoffs to call out: 1) security boundary — do we allow the shim to hold customer credentials? 2) observability — how do we surface tenant tracing/metrics consistently when parts run local vs hosted? @maria any proposals?

maria: For (1) we should avoid shim-stored long-term creds in Hosted. Use delegated short-lived tokens. For Private, run a local agent that talks to customer KMS inside the network so creds never leave their boundary. For (2) include a telemetry adapter: local agent emits standardized tags (tenant_id, deployment_mode, shim_version) that the control plane ingests when available.

sanjay: Also, version the translator/manifest schema (v1, v2) and keep runtime flags to accept old manifests for a while. Don't force a mass rollout. Breaking behavior changes are painful for customers.

kevin: :thinking_face: add to that — performance overhead. Local agent + translation adds ~5-12ms for cold paths in our microbench; need concrete numbers across model sizes. We'll need perf gates in CI.

deploy-bot: canary deployed translator-v1 to staging for perf tests — https://staging.redwood/api/translate (job #deploy-917)

alex: Good. Action items:
- sanjay: draft the capability matrix (include network, kms, auth, telemetry, rollout hooks)
- maria: spec the minimal thin-shim API + explicit extension hooks for local agent connectors
- kevin: run perf microbench (hosted vs local-agent) and add telemetry tags to bench outputs
I'll consolidate into the RFC follow-up and drop a PR. Thanks all :thumbsup:

(Reaction: sanjay added :eyes:)
